paradigm.name: set-valued diagnosis over calibrated behavioral envelopes
paradigm.question: Which declared physical fault hypotheses remain consistent with the observed multivariate response under measurement uncertainty and a supported operating regime?
paradigm.distinction_from_classifier: Return every admissible hypothesis, not only the highest-scoring class. Overlapping normal/fault envelopes remain ambiguous; no compatible envelope is unknown or out of support.
paradigm.mathematical_rule: A hypothesis h is admissible when, for every required channel j, the distance between the observation interval and the calibrated behavioral interval is no greater than the preregistered, dimensionless calibrated margin.
paradigm.unique_claim: A singleton is unique only within the complete, frozen, independently reviewed hypothesis catalogue. It is not proof of a globally unique physical cause.

envelope_contract.review: Independent calibration review receipt and upstream signer/issuer verification are mandatory; a boolean flag and digest do not authenticate reviewer identity.
envelope_contract.missing_support: Missing, stale, conflicted, unsupported or absent required signals return not_evaluable, never normal.

hard_gates: all hypotheses share the same regime, frozen model, training/calibration split, coverage target and exact signal set
each envelope digest is recomputed before diagnosis
training and calibration recording manifests are disjoint
calibration episode counts meet finite-sample requirements for the declared marginal coverage
every envelope carries an independently reviewed calibration receipt and upstream identity verification
observation channels have current signal-quality status and declared measurement uncertainty
unsupported regimes return not_evaluable rather than being compared with another regime's envelope
missing, stale or conflicted required signals return not_evaluable rather than normal
all compatible hypotheses are returned; the system may not force a top-one diagnosis
zero compatible hypotheses are reported as unknown/out-of-support
singleton uniqueness is explicitly scoped to the frozen declared catalogue
global unique physical cause claims remain prohibited without independent global-identifiability evidence
uncertainty and performance intervals are clustered by independent recording/engine run, not sample rows

comparators.method: Select the highest class score regardless of envelope overlap; report confidence and unsupported behavior.
Calibrated top-one classifier with abstention threshold.
Independent per-channel residual thresholds, union rule.
Joint covariance residual ellipsoid with frozen covariance and calibrated threshold.
Proposed set-valued intersection of calibrated multivariate behavioral envelopes and observation intervals.

stress_cases: two physically distinct faults produce overlapping response envelopes
normal operating regime overlaps a fault envelope under ambient shift
one missing or conflicted channel removes identifiability
an unseen condition lies outside every calibrated envelope
two hypotheses are admissible but a softmax classifier picks one
one model parameter set has a nontrivial observational equivalence class
the declared catalogue omits the true physical cause

research_targets_not_achieved.target: Zero forced top-one diagnoses when more than one calibrated envelope remains admissible.
At least 95% detection of held-out out-of-support episodes at no more than 1% false unknown alarms on supported normal episodes, with recording-clustered uncertainty.
Empirical behavioral-envelope coverage within ±5 percentage points of the preregistered marginal target on independent test recordings.
At least 5 percentage points better event-level fault recall than a matched selective classifier without increasing false alarms per observed normal hour, while maintaining ambiguity-set coverage.

limitations.catalogue_completeness: A singleton is only as sound as the declared hypothesis catalogue. Omitted mechanisms can still explain the observation.
limitations.calibration: Finite-sample marginal coverage assumes exchangeability of independent calibration episodes; this is not guaranteed under regime/fault shift.
limitations.global_identifiability: Local envelope disjointness within one regime does not establish global physical uniqueness.
limitations.claim_ceiling: Source contract and synthetic fixtures only; no trained model, public-dataset result, or physical diagnostic claim.
